inputs.original_text: ISRAEL’S parliament began a debate today on a Bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. The Bill’s passage would be a victory for Israel’s far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of the religious party that introduced the legislation. Opponents of the legislation call it racist, draconian and unlikely to deter attacks by Palestinian militants.
inputs.modified_text: This is not really about deterring attacks. The bill would make death the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis, while the security argument is a convenient pitch for enshrining unequal justice in law. Ben-Gvir’s religious party introduced it, but the bigger prize is making an extreme use of state power seem like ordinary policy. Even debating it helps normalize it; opponents’ denunciations don’t change what the process is doing.
